fieldMarks: 11-14.5 in; adult mostly purple and green with a pale blue frontal shield above a red-and-yellow bill.
Bright yellow legs and long toes; white undertail coverts.
Immature much plainer, buff-brown and olive; note bill shape and white undertail.
behavior: Walks on lily pads, runs on open shorelines and clambers through marsh vegetation and waterside trees, flicking its short tail.
Nods its head as it swims; flies short distances with legs dangling.
Omnivorous: seeds, fruits and leaves plus insects, frogs, snails and fish; sometimes eggs and young of other birds.
habitat: Extensive fresh wetlands with still or slow shallow water, dense marsh cover and floating vegetation such as lily pads.
range: Breeds in the southeastern United States and Texas and withdraws in winter mostly to southern Florida; strays wander north as far as Canada at any season.
